summary: No training data or wellness metrics have been recorded over the past 4 weeks, making it impossible to assess current fitness, fatigue, or adherence to the plan. With a Marathon 85 days away (target sub-4h at ~5:45/km), this is a critical build phase and the absence of logged activity is a concern that needs immediate attention. The upcoming plan is well-structured for Ironman base building, but marathon-specific pace work at 5:45/km should be woven in more deliberately given the race proximity.
suggestions: Start logging all sessions immediately — without data from your watch or manual entries, it's impossible to track fitness trends or catch early signs of overtraining or underrecovery ahead of your marathon in 85 days.

With the marathon 85 days away, your Tuesday interval session (6x800m @ 4:55–5:10/km on 17 Nov) is valuable, but add one weekly tempo run specifically at 5:35–5:50/km sustained for 30–40 min to build race-pace confidence at your 5:45/km marathon target.

Long run distances of 20–21km are appropriate for this phase, but aim to include the final 3–5km of each long run at or close to marathon pace (5:45/km) to practise negative-splitting and race-pace feel without adding extra volume.

Malta's November conditions are mild and runnable — take advantage of cooler morning temperatures for long runs to simulate more typical marathon race conditions and build heat tolerance awareness for Ironman Italy next June.

Prioritise sleep tracking — re-sync your Garmin device or manually log sleep scores so recovery can be properly monitored; with no wellness data available, there is no way to gauge readiness before hard sessions.

proposed_changes.reason: With the marathon 85 days away, introducing a race-pace finish to the long run builds specific neuromuscular and metabolic adaptation at target pace without adding volume stress.

proposed_changes.reason: Keeping Thursday tempo efforts at the marathon-adjacent pace band (vs. faster 5:35/km end) sharpens specificity for the sub-4h marathon without over-stressing the system mid-build.
